examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability of a Normal Random Variable on an Unbounded Interval
examples.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

$$
P(X <       x) = P \left( Z <       \dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma} \right)
$$

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = 2$ and $\sigma = 2.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.24) & =P(Z<\frac{1.24-2}{2}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.38) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.38) \\  & =Φ(-0.38)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/48d92806543cb86b2906032b1723fa942db842e7f283681cafeeb9b11fca8cab.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
\Phi(-0.38) = 0.3520.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X <               1.24) = 0.3520.
$$
